messages:
marta: quick follow-up from the runaway-tenant postmortem — we need a concrete resilience roadmap for the continuous batcher. TL;DR: minimize latency regressions while ensuring noisy tenants can't saturate KV cache. Thoughts?

jonathan: +1. we should formalize fallback to microbatching when headroom < 20% and kv_warmup_rate < 0.5, but exact thresholds need experiments.

lia: agree. also need an escape hatch for TTL-driven eviction spikes. current hysteresis flips too fast and we get oscillation.

kevin: proposal: three-tier fallback policy: 1) slow-path microbatching (reduce grouping window), 2) degraded model variant (quantized / smaller context), 3) route to dedicated pool / lower-priority queue. each action must emit a metric and a cooldown.

jonathan: love the tiers. we should define the signals precisely: headroom_pct, inflight_batches, kv_miss_rate, enqueue_latency_p50 and p99, and model_token_rate.

marta: can we avoid cross-component coupling? i.e., scheduler/batcher shouldn't hardcode model variants. prefer a policy layer that decides actions and a router that executes them.

lia: policy layer makes sense. quick interface sketch: 
```
FallbackPolicy {
  signals: ["headroom_pct", "kv_miss_rate"],
  action: "microbatch" | "variant_swap" | "route_dedicated",
  cooldown_s: 30,
  min_duration_s: 5
}
```
We can store per-tenant policies and version them.

kevin: question about admission/eviction: do we move preemptive eviction into the allocator (resource owner) or keep it inside the batcher? moving into allocator centralizes resource decisions but complicates batching handoffs.

jonathan: allocator owns tokens/units; batcher owns grouping and kv-cache usage. my vote: allocator makes eviction decisions, batcher exposes `drain_hint()` and `fastpath_small_request()` hooks so decisions are enacted cleanly.

marta: sample drain_hint API idea: 
```
// from batcher -> allocator
drain_hint(tenant_id, priority, target_units, reason) -> {granted_units: int, force_evict: bool}
```
allocator can return smaller units or instruct batcher to evict lowest-priority inflight.

lia: ops requirements: add telemetry for headroom timelines (per-tenant), fallback_counts, fallback_duration_histogram, and kv_warmup_success_rate. these will be critical for postmortem/rollback signals.

infra-bot: deploy-bot: canary deploy scheduled for 1776543300. Canary will include batcher hooks + allocator drain_hint stub.

kevin: testing plan: synthetic noisy-tenant test that injects KV misses and enqueues 50k tiny requests/sec. Expect fallback to microbatch within ~5s and p99 latency degrade <2x. Also validate cooldown prevents flip-flopping.

jonathan: also add chaos test: partial KV backend outage -> ensure we gracefully route traffic to degraded variant or dedicated pool, not full outage.

marta: OK owners/next steps: jonathan -> implement drain_hint + batcher hooks (2w); lia -> telemetry + SLO dashboard (1w); kevin -> policy spec and canary tests (1w). I'll write a short RFC and coordinate rollout.

sre-bot: incident-bot: created follow-up INC-2026 to monitor fallback events and alert if fallback_rate > 1% sustained for 5m.

marta: thanks all. sync tomorrow 10am in #eng-runtime to review canary results. :rocket:
